passage:
Imran: saw Sana's story. she's with someone new
Parveen: oh Imran. how are you doing?
Imran: stung. like, actually stung. I typed a whole post to make her look
Parveen: did you send it?
Imran: no. deleted it 😔
Imran: I keep looking at his profile. comparing. his jaw, his job
Parveen: that's the worst game. you never win
Parveen: want to mute her right now while I'm here? I'll sit with you
Imran: ok. doing it
Imran: done. feels weird
Parveen: weird is fine. her being happy isn't a verdict on you
Imran: I know. I don't feel it yet
Parveen: you don't have to. come get chai? 🤍

qa.q: What did Imran type but then delete?
qa.a: Imran typed a whole post to make Sana look bad, then deleted it.

qa.q: What might Imran be feeling as he keeps looking at the new partner's profile?
qa.a: Imran seems hurt and insecure and keeps comparing, since Imran says 'actually stung' and keeps checking the other person's jaw and job.

qa.q: What step did Imran take that helped, and what else could Imran do?
qa.a: Imran muted Sana with Parveen close by; Imran could also let the pain pass with friends and avoid checking the new profile or contacting the new partner.

qa.q: Why might Parveen say that weird is fine after Imran mutes Sana?
qa.a: Parveen knows that feeling odd after a hard step is normal, and wants Imran to know there is no need to feel better instantly.

grounding: Shows the sting of an ex's new partner, with the person resisting a provoking post, muting, and being reminded it is no verdict on them.

passage: Dhruv was on the metro to Indiranagar when the photo came up: Jyoti, laughing on a beach in Gokarna, arm around a tall guy in a red cap. Four months since she'd ended things. The sting was sharp and physical, like missing a step. By the time he reached his stop, he had opened the guy's profile, counted his followers, and drafted a story of himself at a rooftop party, just to show he was fine. He stood on the platform with his thumb over 'post'. Then he thought: who is this for? Not for him. It was for Jyoti to see, and maybe to sting her back. He deleted the draft. He muted Jyoti and the man in the red cap and put the phone away. At home he called his friend Aakash and admitted, 'It hurts more than I thought.' Aakash said, 'It will, for a while. Her being happy doesn't mean you weren't enough.' Dhruv sat with that. It helped a little.

qa.q: Where was Jyoti in the photo?
What did Dhruv feel when he saw the photo?
qa.a: A sharp, physical sting of jealousy and hurt, like missing a step.

qa.q: What did Dhruv do instead of posting to provoke?
qa.a: He deleted the draft, muted Jyoti and her new partner, and called Aakash to admit the hurt.

qa.q: How does Aakash see Jyoti's new happiness?
qa.a: As no verdict on Dhruv; her being happy doesn't mean he wasn't enough.

grounding: Shows a young man stung by his ex's new partner, resisting comparison and provocation, muting them and letting the pain pass.

passage:
'He's here with her,' Vasudha whispered, gripping Maria's arm at the college fest. Across the lawn, her ex, Kunal, was sharing a plate of momos with a girl in a green kurta.
'Okay. Breathe,' Maria said. 'Want to leave?'
'No. Yes. I don't know.' Vasudha's eyes were stinging. 'She's so pretty. What does she have that I didn't?'
'Stop right there. This isn't a competition.'
'I'm going to message her. Just to say hi. Just to see.'
'Vasu. Just to see what? To make her uncomfortable? To make him notice you?'
Vasudha stared at her phone. 'Maybe.'
'Then no. You'd hate yourself tomorrow.'
Vasudha put the phone away, slowly. 'It really hurts.'
'I know. Let it hurt. It'll pass. And him being happy doesn't mean you weren't worth it.'
'Can we get chaat on the other side of the fest?'
'And mute him on the way.'
'Both. Yes.'

qa.q: What was Kunal sharing with the girl in the green kurta?
What was Vasudha feeling when she saw Kunal with someone new?
qa.a: Her eyes stung with hurt and jealousy, and she compared herself to the new girl.

qa.q: How did Maria help Vasudha avoid a mistake?
qa.a: She asked what messaging the new girl was really for, and steered Vasudha to let it hurt, mute Kunal and go for chaat.

qa.q: How might the girl in the green kurta feel if Vasudha had messaged her?
qa.a: Probably uncomfortable and confused, pulled into something that wasn't about her.

grounding: Shows a young woman stung by her ex's new partner, choosing not to compare or contact her, and letting the pain pass with a friend.
